name: ChipGroup
purpose: Lay out a wrapping row of Chips at one shared size and alignment.
intent: Give a row of Chips its measured wrap, gap, and alignment in one place, and remove the repetition (and the silent misalignment) of setting the same size on every chip by hand.

sourceFiles.note: The shared size is provided through ChipSizeContext, which lives with Chip (chip/chip-size-context.ts) rather than here, so Chip can consume it without importing its own group.

figmaSource.note: Filed on the file's own "✅⏲️ Chip Group" page, verified directly against the file via the Desktop Bridge plugin.
figmaSource.structure: Four variants cross `size` (`sm (24)` / `md (32)`) with `alignment` (left/right). Every variant is a single auto-layout frame - layoutMode HORIZONTAL, layoutWrap WRAP, itemSpacing 8, counterAxisSpacing 8, counterAxisAlignItems CENTER, and zero padding - containing ten `chip` instances, all `mode=scope`, `isSelected=false`, each carrying the variant's own size. `alignment=left` measures primaryAxisAlignItems MIN; `alignment=right` measures MAX. There is no overflow instance, no divider, and no container fill or stroke: the group is pure layout.
apiAdaptationNotes: Chip Group takes `children`, not a data array. Tag Group and Avatar Group own their items because they have to decide which are visible and which are truncated; Chip Group has no overflow behaviour at all, and Chip's own props are a discriminated union on `mode`, which a flat item type could not express without duplicating that union. Button Group - the closest analogue in this system - is likewise a children-based layout wrapper.

`size` reaches each Chip through React context (ChipSizeContext), not by cloning children. cloneElement only reaches direct children, so a Chip inside a Tooltip, returned from a `.map`, or rendered conditionally would silently miss the group's size - the same structural fragility that detached Chip's own remove button from its pill. Context reaches any descendant regardless of what sits between, and an explicit `size` on an individual Chip still wins because Chip resolves `size ?? groupSize ?? 'md'`.
The provider is only mounted when `size` is actually set, so a Chip Group without one leaves every Chip on its own default rather than overriding it with undefined.

`alignment` is genuinely different from Tag Group's identically-named prop despite the shared axis name. Here it maps to Figma's primaryAxisAlignItems MIN/MAX - literally which edge the chips pack against (justify-content). In Tag Group it decides where the overflow tag renders. Chip Group has no overflow, so there is nothing to place.
No overflow or truncation was implemented, because Figma models none - all ten chips in every variant are plain, equal siblings. Chip Group is deliberately not Tag Group with chips in it.

Chip Group never manages selection. Figma's variants are all `isSelected=false` scope chips, and scope chips are independent on/off toggles - so any one-of-N coordination belongs to the consumer holding the state, exactly as with Toggle Button.
`role="group"` is applied only when an accessible name is given (aria-label/aria-labelledby), matching Button Group - an unnamed group is a boundary a screen-reader user steps through for no benefit.

useCases: A row of selectable search scopes above a results list
A bar of active filter chips above a task or matter list
Any wrapping collection of chips that should share one size
antiPatterns: A group needing overflow truncation behind a "+N more" affordance - that is Tag Group's job, with Tags
A row of buttons - use Button Group
Managing which chip is selected - Chip Group is layout only; hold that state yourself

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.description: A wrapping flex row with an 8px gap on both axes and no padding or surface of its own. Carries data-alignment and data-size.

anatomy.name: children
anatomy.description: The Chips. Any element is accepted, but the layout is built for Chip.

size.description: Shared by every Chip inside, via context. Omit to leave each Chip on its own default. An explicit size on an individual Chip wins.

alignment.description: Which edge the chips pack against - maps to justify-content.

aria-label.description: Names the group and makes it announced as role="group".

className.description: Composes with the root's class list.

left.purpose: Chips pack against the inline start. The default, and Figma's own first variant.

right.purpose: Chips pack against the inline end.

accessibility.role: group, but only when aria-label or aria-labelledby is provided - an unnamed group adds a boundary with no benefit
accessibility.focusOrder: DOM order of the children; Chip Group adds no roving tabindex or arrow-key handling, because its children are independent controls rather than a single composite widget
accessibility.selection: not managed - each scope Chip carries its own aria-pressed
accessibility.note: Chip Group renders no interactive element of its own, so it has no focus or keyboard behaviour to document beyond its children's.

keyboardInteraction: Tab moves between the Chips' own controls in DOM order
All other keyboard behaviour belongs to the individual Chips (Enter/Space, Escape to close a segment menu, arrow keys inside an open menu)
behaviorRules: Provides `size` to descendant Chips through context; an explicit per-Chip size wins.
Mounts the size provider only when `size` is set.
Never coordinates selection or removal between chips.
Applies no padding, background, or border of its own - every visible pixel belongs to the Chips.
compositionRules: Pass Chips as children; wrappers are fine - context reaches through them, unlike prop cloning.
Hold scope selection and filter removal in the consumer, and pass them down to each Chip.
Use Tag Group instead when the group needs truncation behind a "+N more" affordance.
responsiveRules: Chips wrap onto new lines once the row runs out of inline space, keeping the same 8px gap on both axes.
The group hugs its container's width; `alignment` decides which edge partial rows pack against.
themeRules: No colour of its own - fully inherited from the Chips inside. Verified in both themes.

tokens.note: chip-group.module.css references exactly one token - gap: var(--spacing-sm), matching Figma's measured itemSpacing 8 and counterAxisSpacing 8 on both axes. Everything else is layout keywords. No colour, padding, or border tokens, by design.

do: Set `size` once on the group rather than on every Chip - a missed chip in a wrapping row misaligns the whole line.
Give the group an aria-label when it forms a meaningful set ("Search scopes", "Active filters").
dont: Do not expect overflow truncation - Figma models none; reach for Tag Group if you need it.
Do not expect Chip Group to manage which chips are selected.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders its children in a wrapping row with an 8px gap on both axes.
alignment=left packs chips against the inline start; alignment=right against the inline end.
size applies to every Chip inside, including ones behind a wrapper or produced by a map.
An explicit size on an individual Chip wins over the group's.
With no size set, each Chip keeps its own default.
Announced as role="group" only when it has an accessible name.
Forwards a ref and passes native div attributes through.
Adds no padding, background, or border of its own.
knownLimitations: No overflow or truncation - Figma models none. A very long filter bar wraps rather than collapsing behind a "+N more" chip.
No roving tabindex: every Chip's controls are individually tabbable, which is correct for independent controls but makes a very large group long to tab through.
futureEnhancements: Overflow truncation behind a "+N more" chip, if a real filter bar needs it - would need a Figma variant first.
A vertical orientation, if chips ever stack; Figma models horizontal only.
